proof:
The derivative of $P$ is positive on $[0,\infty)$, and exact substitution gives $P(2/3)=-239945/243<0$ and $P(3/4)=1198965/1024>0$. Hence the unique positive root satisfies $2/3<c<3/4$. The $a_j$ are positive affine and at most $1$, and $a_8>6/7$ since $7(8+c)-6(9+c)=2+c>0$. The sequence $v$ is constant and satisfies all its constraints. Expanding the finite sum yields $\sum_{j=0}^9(j-8)(j+c)^5=-P(c)$, so the critical balance holds exactly after division by $(9+c)^5$.

For $j<9$ the ratio $(j+c)/(9+c)$ increases with $c$, and the term at $j=9$ is constant. Thus
$$
\sum_j a_j^6<\sum_{j=0}^9\left(\frac{4j+3}{39}\right)^6
=\frac{2280098630}{1172914587}<\frac{39}{20}
<5\left(\frac67\right)^6 .
$$
The two strict rational comparisons follow by cross multiplication from $39\cdot1172914587-20\cdot2280098630=141696293$ and $100\cdot6^6-39\cdot7^6=77289$. Since $\sum_jv_j^6=10$, the claimed inequality is reversed strictly.

For the polynomial assertion, put $k=a_8$ and $\delta=(1-k)/k=t_*$. Then $a_j/k=1+t_*(j-8)$ and $\Phi'(t_*)=0$ by critical balance. The left endpoint $e=-1$ of the nonnegative-root slope interval $[-1,1/8]$ gives $1+e(j-8)=9-j\ge0$ on all sites. The expression $a_j/k+\delta[1+e(j-8)]$ equals the constant $1/k=v_j/k$, by direct substitution. Since $0<\delta<1/6$, increasing $\delta$ to $1/6$ weakly increases every such root and gives $(7/6)[1+((6t_*+e)/7)(j-8)]$. Taking sixth powers and summing, the strict inequality $\sum_jv_j^6>(2/\Gamma_6)\sum_ja_j^6$ implies $(7/6)^6\Phi((6t_*+e)/7)> (2/\Gamma_6)\Phi(t_*)$. Cancelling $(7/6)^6=1/\Gamma_6$ proves the assertion.

statement:
The following scalar inequality fails. On $j=0,\ldots,R$, suppose $a_j$ is a positive affine sequence, $a_i\ge d/(d+1)$, and $\sum_j(j-i)a_j^{d-1}=0$. Suppose $v$ is a positive concave sequence with $v\ge a$ and $v_i=1$. The claimed bound is $\sum_jv_j^d\le(2/\Gamma_d)\sum_ja_j^d$, with $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.

A counterexample has $d=6$, $R=9$, $i=8$, $a_j=(j+c)/(9+c)$ and $v_j=1$, where $c$ is the unique positive root of
$$
P(c)=35c^5+375c^4+2550c^3+8670c^2+9195c-11805.
$$
In the corresponding polynomial $\Phi(t)=\sum_{j=0}^9[1+t(j-8)]^6$, the critical slope is $t_*=1/(8+c)$, and for the endpoint $e=-1$ of the nonnegative-root slope interval one has $\Phi((6t_*+e)/7)>2\Phi(t_*)$.
title: A ten-site counterexample to the critical affine-root moment bound
